decision_reason: A1 already provides useful global intensity, temporal, impact, orientation, rotation and translation concepts, but it under-specifies where motion and posture changes occur. This particularly limits transferable separation of cycling, which has the weakest seen-prototype coverage, and of waist bends forward, cycling and climbing stairs, which have the lowest unseen-neighbor margins. Splitting global posture variability into trunk and instrumented-limb components separates waist flexion from limb-dominant motion, while upper- and lower-limb motion intensity provide supported regional contrasts anchored by frontal elevation of arms and the seen locomotor classes.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: trunk_posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the chest and trunk configuration changes relative to gravity within a window.

attributes.name: limb_posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the gravity-relative orientations of the instrumented lower arm and ankle segments change within a window.

levels.Low: Instrumented limb orientations remain nearly constant.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: upper_limb_motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Magnitude and energy of motion expressed by the instrumented right lower arm, independently of overall body-motion intensity.

levels.Low: Weak or nearly absent lower-arm motion.
levels.Medium: Moderate lower-arm motion magnitude and energy.

attributes.name: lower_limb_motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Magnitude and energy of motion expressed by the instrumented left ankle, independently of overall body-motion intensity.

levels.Low: Weak or nearly absent ankle motion.
levels.Medium: Moderate ankle motion magnitude and energy.

operations.reason: Global motion energy remains a direct, sensor-supported distinction between static postures, moderate exercises and vigorous locomotion; regional additions describe distribution rather than replace this whole-body scale.
Repetition rate is physically distinct from motion magnitude and helps transfer from periodic seen locomotion to climbing stairs and cycling.
Sustained rapid fluctuation is independently supported by jerk-related motion structure and contrasts smooth cyclic or bending motions with less smooth impact-rich locomotion.
Short high-magnitude changes remain distinct from sustained intensity and provide an impact contrast grounded by running and jumping.

Mean gravity-relative load-bearing posture provides the principal transferable distinction between standing still and the seen sitting and lying postures, while also characterizing inclined activities.

The original global measure conflates trunk reorientation with local limb reorientation. Chest gravity-angle variation can identify trunk-dominant waist bending, while lower-arm and ankle orientation changes transfer from arm elevation, crouching and locomotion to limb-dominant cycling and stair climbing.
Angular-motion prominence remains a general modality-supported contrast between static or primarily translational activities and bending, arm elevation, crouching or cycling.
Sustained locomotor progression is distinct from local segment motion and preserves transfer from walking, jogging and running to climbing stairs.

Temporal predictability is physically separate from repetition rate because motions with similar cadence can differ in cycle consistency; it remains transferable across repetitive seen and unseen activities.

Lower-arm accelerometer and gyroscope measurements support a regional motion-energy attribute. The seen frontal elevation of arms supplies a clear upper-limb-dominant anchor, helping distinguish waist bends forward from arm-dominant rotation and cycling from activities with vigorous arm movement.

Ankle accelerometer and gyroscope measurements support a regional lower-limb energy attribute. Seen walking, jogging, running, crouching and jumping provide transferable anchors for the pronounced lower-limb motion expected in cycling and climbing stairs.

semantic_redundancy_review: The final attributes separate whole-body magnitude, repetition rate, sustained fluctuation, isolated impacts, mean global posture, regional posture change, angular motion, locomotor translation, temporal predictability and regional motion energy. Smoothness is not merged with impulsiveness because sustained jerk and isolated peaks are different physical properties. Cadence is not merged with motion_regularity because repetition speed and cycle consistency are independent. Posture_inclination measures mean global configuration, whereas trunk_posture_variability and limb_posture_variability measure time-varying regional orientation. Upper- and lower-limb motion intensity overlap operationally with global motion_intensity only in their shared energy basis; they are retained because their regional distribution supplies independent, sensor-supported contrasts for cycling, waist bending, stair climbing and arm elevation. Rotational_motion is retained as a motion-type measure rather than a regional energy measure, and translational_motion remains specific to sustained progression.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
